one_sentence_story: Pain does not race up a fixed wire to your head. Fast touch nerves from rubbing a shin beat slow ache nerves and shut a gate in your spine.
so_what_for_you: Pair firm rubbing or warmth with a slow breath when pain flares. You shut your spinal pain gate from skin and brain at once.

jargon_map.plain: A nerve gate in the back of your spine that turns pain up or down.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a tollgate blocking slow cars before the highway.

jargon_map.plain: Thick fast nerves that carry touch and rubbing up your leg in a flash.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a fast train beating slow cars to the gate.

jargon_map.plain: Thin slow nerves that carry dull ache at two meters per second.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a slow bike reaching a gate that is already shut.

jargon_map.plain: Calm signals from your brainstem that move down your spine to quiet pain.
jargon_map.analogy: Like turning down the sound with a remote.
